Yehonatan Malka, son of Ronit and Moshe Nissim, was born on 21 Adar I 5760 (27 February 2000). He was one of triplets, together with Ariel and Shira, and the three of them were siblings to Michael and Daniel.

Yehonatan (Yoni) grew up and was educated in Beersheba. From a young age he was marked by gentleness, modesty, good faith and a love of nature. Yoni studied at the Chabad educational institutions in Beersheba, and in high school he moved to study at the Shomriya high yeshiva. At the yeshiva Yoni developed and shaped his character. His friends spoke of his good heart and his interest in everyone around him; of his care to find merit in each person; and of his guarding of his speech and avoidance of all gossip and negative talk.

Yoni stood out in his love for every living creature he came across, from tiny ants, whose peace he took care not to disturb, to injured birds, which he looked after until they recovered and returned to nature. During his yeshiva years Yoni ran an animal corner and also served as an older guide for the younger students who joined the yeshiva. From Shomriya he moved to study at Neta Yimincha, an agricultural yeshiva in Ashtemoa that combines Torah study with farm work. Studies at the yeshiva demanded great diligence, rising early in the morning and physical labor in difficult weather, alongside Torah study in the later hours of the day. Yoni saw this way of life as a privilege, and even considered returning to the yeshiva after completing his military service.

Those who loved him described him as "a rare blend of love of the Land of Israel, love of the people of Israel and love of the Torah." A smiling young man with a pleasant manner, always welcoming and content with his lot, he stood out above all for the humility and gentleness that characterized his conduct. His large heart had room for everyone, and he was ready to listen to others with a sincere and devoted attention, which brought great comfort in itself, even apart from any advice he later gave.

The commandment "love your neighbor as yourself" was a lamp to his feet, and the love he gave to others came back to him from them. He was loved by all, and left a unique impression on everyone who knew him.

Yoni loved nature in all its forms: springs, water pools, hiking trails, plants and animals. He pursued bird ringing as a hobby and dreamed of becoming a therapeutic riding instructor at a horse farm. Yoni also loved making coffee and had his own special coffee setup, which he constantly invested in and upgraded to pamper his friends. He enjoyed sharing fine drinks with the family, and was the one responsible for pouring the drinks into everyone's glasses, raising a "l'chaim" with the smile that was reserved for him alone.

Upon completing his studies at the higher yeshiva, he enlisted in the IDF and volunteered for full military service as a combat soldier in the Armored Corps. He completed various training courses and served as a tank loader in the Yiftach Gedud (Yigal) Battalion... in the 82nd Battalion of the 7th Armored Brigade, "Saar MiGolan." His commanders described him as a highly motivated and dedicated soldier who felt a deep sense of mission in his military service. In his notebook he wrote: "A fighter does not do what he loves; he finds the love in what he does." This was the motto by which he lived.

On Shabbat, 22 Tishrei, Simchat Torah 5784, 7 October 2023, at half past six in the morning, the terrorist organization Hamas launched a surprise attack on Israel. Under cover of massive rocket and missile fire from the Gaza Strip into wide areas of the country, thousands of terrorists broke in by land, sea and air, and began a murderous assault on the communities of the Gaza envelope and on everyone in the area. That morning, a war began.

At the outbreak of the war Yoni was at home, temporarily attached to the reserve unit 2 until he recovered from a leg injury. His discharge was due to begin after the holidays, timed to his expected recovery date, so he assumed he would no longer return to the company and would be discharged from his unit. However, once he understood the gravity of the hour, Yoni did everything in his power to be reattached to his unit, to obtain the required equipment, and to join his comrades, who by then had entered combat in Gaza. Yoni surprised his commander, who encountered him in the Gaza Strip without understanding how he had gotten in. Together with his friends he fought as a loader in the tank until the first ceasefire. When he left the Strip, he and the members of his cohort were given the chance to leave the company and go home, as they were already officially discharged from regular service. Yet Yoni did not want to leave his comrades at these fateful moments; as a veteran soldier he felt responsibility toward his crew and chose to stay with them. Despite further opportunities that came his way, Yoni refused to go home and insisted on staying to contribute his share.

Even during the fighting his sensitivity did not dull. His mother said: "Yoni had immense sensitivity, but at the same time he was also a great 'fighter.' This combination found expression in his ability to be a tank fighter while being sensitive toward every small creature. Once, when he went home for a short time, he heard a cat trapped deep inside a sewage shaft. Yoni spent many hours getting it out, and did not rest until he had cleaned and fed it and made sure it was all right. This is the conduct that characterized him."

On 5 December 2023, during fighting in Khan Yunis aimed at bringing the hostages back from Hamas captivity, an anti-tank missile struck his tank, and Yoni was killed.

Sergeant First Class Yehonatan Malka fell in battle on 22 Kislev 5784 (5 December 2023), aged twenty-three. He was laid to rest in the Military Cemetery on Mount Herzl in Jerusalem. He is survived by his parents, a sister and three brothers.

After his death he was posthumously promoted to Sergeant Major.

His father eulogized him: "A sweet youth who became a young and handsome man, sensitive, with the virtues of a righteous person."

His mother eulogized him: "The happiest child in the world, radiant of face, of endless compassion. The gentleness, the nobility, the sweetness and the tenderness are an inseparable part of your being."

Various commemorative initiatives have been held in his memory and continue to be held, all in his spirit, with the intention of adding to and spreading his light in this complex period in the history of our people.

His family established an association in his memory, "Keshet Yehonatan Lo Nasog Achor" ("Yehonatan's Bow Will Not Retreat"), through which it coordinates the activity.

Among other things, a synagogue named "Keshet Yehonatan" was dedicated in the city of Katowice, Poland. The synagogue is located within an "Israeli House" intended to serve the students studying there and give them the feeling of a warm home while abroad.

A special charity fair in his memory was held at the Ami"t high school in Beersheba, led by Yoni's mother, who manages the senior division at the school. Agricultural produce from the fields of the Gaza envelope was sold at the fair, and the funds raised were designated for continued commemoration.

At Ami"t high school a study hall named "Achi Yehonatan" was established, intended to bring students together with texts from the Jewish library in the spirit of the times, in order to build bridges and connect the different groups in Israeli society.
